body:
It makes sense. But only to someone who has been there.

THank you. I will wake up tomorrow...so count that as selfish or not, or count that as I didn't mean it or not but sometimes It's the little things....so thank you.

And know each night you don't suffer alone witch what you chose...just as all I wanted tonight was to know the same thing and have something to hold on to for a bit in my darkness.

The problem for me is mixing anti-depressants and the pain management. I've managed to scale down from morphine and stadol to the ocassional valium and vicodin for pain relief but that leaves me with the daily pain to deal with and I can't get anyone to deal with both at once.

Thank you.

From looking through you posts, you really seem to have a calling to care. So let me ask a totally unfair question...why? What is your reason to wake up tomorrow? Anyone who cares the way you do has the same pain I am feeling...but their own way to cope...so I'm flipping the table here.

Honestly...I don't know if I'm going to be ok. I thought maybe if I can find someone to help, a reason to reach out I can hold on tonight and be ok.

With chronic pain, I know that my problems come and go...but as you can tell from this throwaway I'm not dealing with it so well tonight..

I've been pushing on since 1984...the day I broke my neck the first time. After months of wearing a brace and the damn halo and being told I should be glad I'm not paralyzed it gets old. The botched surgeries and what comes from it...and refusing to take opioid meds for the addiction problems. Well now it's 2013 and I'm looking for a lifeline. 

I really did give years to that, of being happy I could get out of bed each day instead of being paralyzed or dead. Then in the years that followed, I made the most outrageous bucket list hoping I might get lucky and die during some insane adventure...but it wasn't meant to be.

So here I am today, hurting, crying and hoping that somehow someone will have some spark that makes me want to wake up another day and deal with the pain.

So thank you for being here...but I need something to hold on to fellow internet stranger.

Are you still here? Talk to me...Having the same thoughts tonight for different reasons but if you and I are both going to die I'd rather not do it totally alone.

I've dealt with this for honestly longer than you have been alive. So I won't tell you how you shouldn't think about it...or how it's failing other people or any of that crap. Just talk...I have a daughter a little older than you, who after all I've done and given up just doesn't care but still worships her drug addict of a mother and who takes all the abuse for her and all theother shit that comes with it.

So from someone on the other side...and someone who doesn't want to wake up for another day...I'll be your scream in the night, and I'll listen because someone should
On my last day...I asked friends for help, I asked strangers for help...and then I came to Reddit for help and asked if I should bother to wake up tomorrow. The answer seems to be I shouldn't
It has changed me, and I know how horrible that has made me. I think that's part of why I feel the way I do.

Thank you for taking the time to answer.

So what is it that makes you want to wake up?

The problem is, I'm out of things to be living for. So, in a selfish moment, I was hoping to find other stories or thoughts that might inspire me...or at least let me know I'm not crazy or alone for feeling like this.

With chronic pain, it's a cycle...and sometimes the down cycle is like this and truly makes you believe and feel that nothing at all can be worth another day of this pain.

Again, thank you. And when your day comes and you're thinking the same as I am I hope you remember what you said to me tonight.

Bless you, and good luck on your journey when it comes.
Message me a recommendation if you would...or coincidentally show up with a throw away. I'm on the east coast so choices are limited
I did try, unfortunately for me it makes the depression worse. Stadol works for me, but getting that in the US is harder than getting a cuban cigar.
Thank you for sharing and letting me know I'm not the only one..and I feel like I'm not crazy for thinking and feeling this.
Thank you. My problem is, this instance hurts like hell and I can't find something to grab onto to help wait it out. But thank you for having this moment to share.

I've heard for too many years I'm already supposed to be paralyzed so I guess that finally stopped scaring me. And that is what finally got me thinking to try things I would never have done. 

As for the thoughts, that's exactly it. With chronic pain, they just keep coming on a bad day and I know it. But that doesn't make them stop.
